chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The person who is approached with a request is free until he promises.

key_terms.الْمَسْؤُولُ: The one asked / The person approached with a request

ai.seo_question: When does a person become obligated to give what they were asked for?
ai.summary: In this maxim from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal and ethical status of voluntary charity (*sadaqat*), emphasizing that the donor retains full autonomy until a specific vow (*nadhr*) or promise is made. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for differentiating between mere generosity and binding obligations, ensuring that giving remains a sincere act of will rather than a forced duty.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 336. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
The person who is approached with a request is free until he promises.
